info.name: Spotter Fuel Route API
info.description:
Fuel route planner API: give it a start and finish in the USA and it returns the driving
route, the cheapest places to refuel along it, and the total fuel cost.

- Vehicle: **500-mile range, 10 mpg**, tank starts empty
- Fuel prices: the supplied `fuel_prices.csv`
- Routing: OSRM public server, **one call per trip**, cached after that
- Geocoding: offline (US Census gazetteer), no API calls

## Setup

1. Start the server: `python manage.py runserver` (after `migrate` and `load_data`, see README).
2. Import this collection and the `Spotter Fuel Route - Local` environment, and select the environment.
   Without it the collection falls back to its own `baseUrl` of `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
3. Run the folders in order with the Collection Runner, or send requests one at a time.

From the command line: `npx newman run postman/spotter-fuel-route.postman_collection.json -e postman/local.postman_environment.json`

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/trips/?start=<location>&finish=<location>`

A location is `City, ST` (`Chicago, IL`) or `lat,lon` (`41.88,-87.63`).

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `start`, `finish` | Resolved coordinates |
| `distance_miles`, `duration_hours` | From OSRM |
| `total_gallons` | `distance_miles / 10` |
| `total_cost` | Sum of all stop costs, USD |
| `fuel_stops[]` | In route order: `station` (name, address, price, location), `mile` marker, `gallons` bought, `cost` |
| `route` | GeoJSON LineString, `[lon, lat]` pairs, a point every half mile |
| `map_url` | The same trip drawn on a map |

### `GET /api/trips/map/?start=...&finish=...`

HTML page with a Leaflet map of the route and numbered stops. Uses the cached plan.

## Tests

Every request has tests. A collection-level script also checks every successful plan
against the business rules (see the *1. Plan a trip* folder), so the numbers are verified,
not only the status codes.

item.name: 2. Map
item.description:
`GET /api/trips/map/` renders the same trip on a Leaflet map (HTML). It reuses the cached
plan, so it costs no extra routing call. **Open these in a browser** (or use Postman's
*Preview* tab) to see the route and the numbered stops.

pm.test("cached map responds in under 300 ms", () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(300));

item.name: 3. Errors
item.description:
Bad input. Status codes:

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Missing parameter, unknown city, wrong format, or a point outside the contiguous USA |
| 405 | Anything but GET |
| 422 | No drivable route, or a stretch longer than 500 miles with no fuel station |
| 502 | The routing service (OSRM) is down |

502 isn't in this folder: it needs OSRM to be down. The automated tests cover it with a
mocked router (`python manage.py test`).

response.name: 400 Bad Request

exec: pm.test("detail says: Unknown US city", () => pm.expect(String(pm.response.json().detail)).to.include("Unknown US city"));
